name: Focke-Wulf FWP 149D
summary: Four-seat liaison and trainer built by Focke-Wulf under licence from Piaggio for the German Air Force; a handful survive as private airplanes in the US.

engines: Single six-cylinder Lycoming GO-480 in a smooth cowl
fuselage: Long glazed cabin seating four or five

tellTales: Four-seat low-wing with a long glazed cabin and a boxy upright tail
Retractable tricycle gear and a flat-six nose

confusedWith.howToTell: The Navion has a long sliding canopy and a rounded tail; the FWP 149D has a boxy cabin and an angular tail.
The Comanche has a more modern, rounded shape with a swept tail; the FWP 149D has a boxier cabin and angular tail.
The Bonanza has a larger, more rounded cabin; the FWP 149D has a boxier, more angular shape.
